core.title: Oncology LLM evaluation: From benchmark performance to clinical readiness.
core.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform increasingly well on medical benchmarks, yet benchmark success does not necessarily establish clinical readiness in oncology. Building on recent critiques of medical LLM evaluation, this Perspective identifies four benchmark-practice mismatches: complete-information benchmarks versus active information gathering, single reference answers versus preference-sensitive decisions, cross-sectional snapshots versus longitudinal disease trajectories, and standalone model performance versus model-in-system readiness. To address these gaps, we propose a four-stage evaluation paradigm progressing from a structured knowledge and reasoning baseline to interactive and dialogue-based evaluation, longitudinal trajectory assessment, and model-in-system evaluation. Grounded in the longitudinal, multimodal, and multidisciplinary nature of oncology care, the framework emphasizes the need to calibrate evaluation to intended use and clinical risk and to sustain assessment through continuous monitoring across the model life cycle. Together, these principles offer an operational and oncology-specific pathway for building progressively stronger evidence of clinical readiness.

core.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
core.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for human-AI interaction usually trains the agent against a single large language model (LLM) that simulates the user. We show that agents trained this way can systematically fail to generalize, and we trace the failure to simulator collapse: the simulator LLM is mode-collapsed, and a policy trained against it learns narrow strategies that exploit the simulator's mode behavior; these strategies transfer poorly to unseen simulators and to real users. We formalize the collapse and propose two solutions. Verbalized Sampling, applied at inference time, samples each simulator reply from a verbalized response distribution. Co-Training, applied during training similar to self-play, co-evolves the simulator as the policy, so the policy cannot exploit the mode behavior. A population variant samples the simulator for each rollout from a pool of recent checkpoints. We validate both solutions on three benchmarks: Persuasion for Good, tau^2-bench, and CooperBench. Verbalized Sampling improves held-out success by up to 9% over single-simulator RL, and Co-Training pushes gains further to 14%; the human study shows similar gain on real users. Both solutions also preserve the policy diversity that collapses under single-simulator RL. Overall, our findings on simulator collapse point to diverse simulators as a requirement for RL agents that serve real users. We release SCOPE, an open-source framework for Population Co-Training in multi-agent RL.

core.title_zh: 一个冻结的模拟器并不够：多智能体强化学习中的模拟器坍缩

article.lead: 用大语言模型模拟用户训练智能体，能否让智能体真正适应不同用户？这篇论文指出，依赖单一模拟器可能带来系统性的泛化失败，并探讨如何通过增加模拟行为的多样性缓解这一问题。

sections.title: 单一用户模拟器为何可能误导训练
paragraphs: 在人机交互的多智能体强化学习中，智能体通常与一个模拟用户的大语言模型进行训练。论文指出，这种设置可能出现“模拟器坍塌”：模拟器的输出模式发生坍塌，策略则学会利用这些模式的狭窄行为。
这种策略不一定能适应未见过的模拟器，也可能难以迁移到真实用户。问题因此不只是模拟器能否生成回复，还涉及训练过程中接触到的用户行为是否足够多样。

sections.title: 从回复采样到模拟器共同训练
paragraphs: 论文形式化描述了模拟器坍塌，并提出两种解决方案。**言语化采样**用于推理阶段：先形成以自然语言表述的回复分布，再从中采样每条模拟器回复。
**共同训练**则用于训练阶段，类似自我博弈，让模拟器与策略共同演化，以避免策略利用固定的模式行为。其群体变体从近期检查点池中为每次 rollout 采样模拟器。论文还发布了用于多智能体强化学习中群体共同训练的开源框架 SCOPE。

sections.title: 未见场景的成功率与策略多样性
paragraphs: 作者在 Persuasion for Good、tau^2-bench 和 CooperBench 上验证了两种方案。摘要报告，相比单模拟器强化学习，言语化采样使留出测试成功率最高提升 9%，共同训练将提升进一步推至 14%。
摘要还称，真实用户研究显示了类似幅度的提升；两种方案也保留了在单模拟器强化学习下会坍塌的策略多样性。这些结果支持关注模拟器多样性，但摘要未给出各基准的逐项结果。

sections.title: 摘要尚不能回答哪些验证细节
paragraphs: 摘要没有报告真实用户研究的样本规模与构成，也未说明留出测试的具体划分、各比较方法的完整设置或结果波动。因此，仅凭摘要难以判断不同用户群体、模拟器和任务条件下的效果范围。

core.title: TOUCAN: Synthesizing 1.5M Tool-Agentic Data from Real-World MCP Environments
core.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are rapidly emerging as powerful systems for automating tasks across domains. Yet progress in the open-source community is constrained by the lack of high quality permissively licensed tool-agentic training data. Existing datasets are limited in diversity, realism, and complexity, particularly regarding multi-tool and multi-turn interactions. To address this gap, we introduce Toucan, which contains 1.5 million trajectories synthesized from nearly 500 real-world Model Context Protocols (MCPs). Unlike prior work, Toucan leverages authentic MCP environments to generate diverse, realistic, and challenging tasks with trajectories involving real tool execution. Our pipeline first produces a broad spectrum of tool-use queries using five distinct models, applies model-based quality filtering, and then generates agentic trajectories with three teacher models using two agentic frameworks. Rigorous rule-based and model-based validation ensures high-quality outputs. We also introduce three extensions to further diversify tasks and simulate multi-turn conversations. Models fine-tuned on Toucan outperform larger closed-source counterparts on the BFCL V3 benchmark and establish a new Pareto optimum on MCP-Universe Bench.

core.title: Too Many Cooks Spoil The Broth: Auditing Multi-Agent LLM Councils For Medical Reasoning
core.abstract: Multi-agent debate among large language models (LLMs) is widely assumed to improve reasoning by letting models correct one another. We audit that assumption for English medical question answering (QA). Five open-weight 4 to 8B medical and generalist LLMs answer 8,402 questions across six benchmarks as a council, measured against the same five prompted individually and a single larger Qwen3-VL-32B, text-only. The council beats every member on five of six datasets, but most of that accuracy is in place before debate runs: 67% of verdicts settle at Round 0, and on five of six those are the more accurate questions. Where debate runs, opinion change concentrates on one anchor; on the hardest benchmark 85% of moves toward it happen while it is wrong. There, agreement is worth less than disagreement: questions all five agree on are correct 6.6% of the time against 14.6% otherwise, tracking a shared bias toward the first option. The council also trails the larger model on four of six by up to 16.2 points, at seven times the model calls for 1.6 times the compute. Agreement among models is a measurement that can be biased, not evidence of correctness.
core.summary: 【摘要】论文审视多智能体辩论是否能改善英语医学问答：五个开放权重模型组成议会，并与各自独立作答及单个更大模型比较。议会在六个数据集中的五个上超过每个成员，但多数裁决在辩论前已确定；最困难基准上，模型意见趋向错误锚点，成员一致也不代表正确。议会在四个数据集上落后于更大模型，同时调用与计算开销更高。摘要未交代完整实验细节，结论的适用范围仍需结合全文核查。[摘要]

core.title_zh: 厨师过多反而坏事：审视多智能体大语言模型议会的医学推理

article.lead: 多个大模型共同讨论，是否真的能让医学问答更准确？这项研究审视模型间的辩论与共识，提醒读者区分“达成一致”和“答案正确”。

sections.title: 医学问答中的多模型共识可靠吗
paragraphs: 多智能体辩论的常见设想是：让大语言模型相互纠错，从而改善推理。本文针对英语医学问答审视这一假设，关注模型最终答对多少，也关注讨论何时以及如何改变答案。

sections.title: 委员会、独立模型与较大模型的比较
paragraphs: 研究让五个开放权重的医学和通用大语言模型组成委员会，回答六个基准中的 8,402 道问题；这些模型的规模为 4 至 8B。比较对象包括同样五个模型分别接受提示时的表现，以及以纯文本方式使用的单个较大模型 Qwen3-VL-32B。

sections.title: 辩论前已有优势，共识也可能出错
paragraphs: 委员会在六个数据集中的五个上胜过每个成员，但其大部分准确表现并非来自后续辩论：67% 的最终判断在第 0 轮就已确定；在六个数据集中的五个上，这部分问题的准确率更高。
在实际发生辩论的情形中，观点变化集中指向一个锚定对象。在最难的基准上，向该对象靠拢的观点变化有 85% 发生在它给出错误答案时。
同一最难基准中，五个模型全部一致的问题，正确率为 6.6%；未全部一致的问题则为 14.6%。这一现象与模型共同偏向第一个选项有关。模型一致因此可能反映共享偏差，而不能直接充当正确性的证据。
委员会在六个数据集中的四个上落后于较大模型，差距最高达 16.2 个百分点；与此同时，委员会使用了七倍的模型调用和 1.6 倍的计算量。

sections.title: 摘要能支持多大范围的判断
paragraphs: 摘要给出了问题总数、基准数量和模型规模，但未说明各基准的样本构成，也未展开各数据集的完整比较结果。仅凭摘要，无法判断这些发现对其他语言、医学任务或模型组合的适用范围。
摘要也未详述辩论流程、锚定对象的具体定义和验证细节。因此，这里报告的是摘要中的比较与关联，不宜据此推断所有多智能体系统都无效，或将共识偏差归因于某个未说明的机制。

sections.title: 阅读启发：把共识视为待核验的信号
paragraphs: 阅读启发：评估多模型问答时，可以留意最终准确率之外的讨论前后变化，并追问一致意见是否伴随共同偏差。进一步阅读论文时，可重点查看辩论流程、各基准的比较结果以及计算成本的统计方式。

core.title: TokenCliff: Benchmarking Output-Token Budget Sensitivity in Multi-Turn LLM Agents
core.abstract: Output-token budgets are a first-order deployment constraint for large language model (LLM) agents, yet existing benchmarks typically evaluate them under a single fixed or generous budget. We introduce TokenCliff, a benchmark for measuring multi-turn agent performance across episode-level output-token budgets. It contains 660 deterministic tasks spanning four capability-oriented domains—file operations, data transformation, tool use, and planning—plus a compositional multi-step split. We propose two budget-sensitivity metrics: Budget Elasticity, which captures robustness across budget levels, and the Cliff Index, which captures the sharpest adjacent-budget performance drop. Evaluating 10 LLMs at five budget levels from 200 to 8,192 tokens yields 33,000 episodes. Results show that (1) accuracy drops by up to 32 percentage points between adjacent budgets; (2) neither peak performance nor larger model size necessarily implies stronger budget elasticity; and (3) budget sensitivity is substantially greater in the evaluated multi-turn setting than in the single-shot diagnostic. Code and data are available in our public repository: https://github.com/BairuiZhang/TokenCliff
core.summary: 【摘要】论文针对现有智能体基准通常采用单一固定或宽裕预算的问题，提出 TokenCliff，用于衡量多轮智能体在不同单次任务输出词元预算下的表现。基准包含660个确定性任务，并提出预算弹性和悬崖指数两项指标。对10个模型、五档预算的评估显示，相邻预算下准确率最多下降32个百分点；峰值表现或模型规模较大也不必然意味着更强的预算弹性。当前仅能依据摘要判断，无法核查任务细节与实验过程。

core.title_zh: TokenCliff：多轮大语言模型智能体输出词元预算敏感性基准

article.lead: 大语言模型智能体在多轮任务中能使用多少输出 token，不只是成本设置，也可能影响任务表现。TokenCliff 将输出预算纳入评测，帮助读者关注模型性能随预算变化的稳定性。

sections.title: 智能体评测为何需要关注输出预算
paragraphs: 输出 token 预算是大语言模型智能体部署的重要约束，但摘要指出，现有基准通常只在单一固定预算或较宽裕的预算下评估。这样的评测视角，难以直接呈现性能随预算变化的情况。
TokenCliff 聚焦多轮智能体，以单次任务全过程的输出 token 预算为评测条件，考察不同预算下的任务表现。

sections.title: 从任务集合到预算敏感性指标
paragraphs: 该基准包含 660 个确定性任务，覆盖文件操作、数据转换、工具使用和规划四个能力导向领域，另有一个组合式多步骤划分。
作者提出两个指标：预算弹性（Budget Elasticity）用于刻画跨预算水平的稳健性；悬崖指数（Cliff Index）用于刻画相邻预算之间最剧烈的性能下降。
评测涉及 10 个大语言模型、从 200 到 8,192 tokens 的五个预算水平，共得到 33,000 个评测回合。

sections.title: 相邻预算间也可能出现性能悬崖
paragraphs: 摘要报告，相邻预算水平之间的准确率降幅最高可达 32 个百分点。这提示读者不能仅凭某个预算下的成绩，推断模型在邻近预算下也有相近表现。
研究还发现，峰值表现更好或模型规模更大，并不必然意味着预算弹性更强。在本次评测中，多轮设置的预算敏感性也明显高于单次作答诊断。

sections.title: 摘要尚不能说明的评测边界
paragraphs: 摘要没有列出具体模型、各任务类别的样本构成，也没有说明组合式多步骤划分的具体内容；因此，仅凭摘要无法判断结果对不同任务和模型的适用范围。
摘要没有给出单次作答诊断的具体设置、两项指标的计算细节或其他验证范围。多轮与单次作答的差异应限于所报告的评测条件理解，不能直接推广到所有应用。

sections.title: 阅读启发：把预算曲线纳入模型选择
paragraphs: 对于需要多轮交互的大语言模型应用，阅读启发是：除了比较最高准确率，也可留意不同输出预算下表现是否稳定，以及相邻预算之间是否存在明显落差。
进一步阅读时，可重点查看预算弹性与悬崖指数如何计算、多轮与单次作答如何比较，以及具体任务和模型如何构成；摘要本身尚不足以回答这些问题。

core.title: T-MAP: Red-Teaming LLM Agents with Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search
core.abstract: While prior red-teaming efforts have focused on eliciting harmful text outputs from large language models (LLMs), such approaches fail to capture agent-specific vulnerabilities that emerge through multi-step tool execution, particularly in rapidly growing ecosystems such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). To address this gap, we propose a trajectory-aware evolutionary search method, T-MAP, which leverages execution trajectories to guide the discovery of adversarial prompts. Our approach enables the automatic generation of attacks that not only bypass safety guardrails but also reliably realize harmful objectives through actual tool interactions. Empirical evaluations across diverse MCP environments demonstrate that T-MAP substantially outperforms baselines in attack realization rate (ARR) and remains effective against frontier models, including GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3.5, and GLM-5, thereby revealing previously underexplored vulnerabilities in autonomous LLM agents. Code is available at https://github.com/pwnhyo/T-MAP.
core.summary: 论文研究大语言模型智能体在多步工具调用中产生的安全风险，提出轨迹感知进化搜索方法 T-MAP。[P1][P2] 方法结合风险类别与攻击风格档案、跨轨迹诊断和工具调用图，以实际行动完成程度评价攻击。[P3][P4] 作者报告其在五种 MCP 环境中的平均攻击实现率为57.8%，并通过消融、多模型及人工评价补充证据。[P5][P7][P8] 结果受沙箱环境和攻击者模型等条件限制，不能直接等同于真实部署风险。[P9]

deep_read.problem: 论文关注传统红队测试难以覆盖的智能体风险：有害后果可能由规划、连续工具调用和环境反馈共同产生，而非单轮文本直接显现。[P1] 作者因此把评估重点转向工具执行是否完成预期有害行动，并区分拒绝、执行错误、部分完成和完全实现。[P5]

papers.title: Oncology LLM evaluation: From benchmark performance to clinical readiness.
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform increasingly well on medical benchmarks, yet benchmark success does not necessarily establish clinical readiness in oncology. Building on recent critiques of medical LLM evaluation, this Perspective identifies four benchmark-practice mismatches: complete-information benchmarks versus active information gathering, single reference answers versus preference-sensitive decisions, cross-sectional snapshots versus longitudinal disease trajectories, and standalone model performance versus model-in-system readiness. To address these gaps, we propose a four-stage evaluation paradigm progressing from a structured knowledge and reasoning baseline to interactive and dialogue-based evaluation, longitudinal trajectory assessment, and model-in-system evaluation. Grounded in the longitudinal, multimodal, and multidisciplinary nature of oncology care, the framework emphasizes the need to calibrate evaluation to intended use and clinical risk and to sustain assessment through continuous monitoring across the model life cycle. Together, these principles offer an operational and oncology-specific pathway for building progressively stronger evidence of clinical readiness.

papers.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
papers.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for human-AI interaction usually trains the agent against a single large language model (LLM) that simulates the user. We show that agents trained this way can systematically fail to generalize, and we trace the failure to simulator collapse: the simulator LLM is mode-collapsed, and a policy trained against it learns narrow strategies that exploit the simulator's mode behavior; these strategies transfer poorly to unseen simulators and to real users. We formalize the collapse and propose two solutions. Verbalized Sampling, applied at inference time, samples each simulator reply from a verbalized response distribution. Co-Training, applied during training similar to self-play, co-evolves the simulator as the policy, so the policy cannot exploit the mode behavior. A population variant samples the simulator for each rollout from a pool of recent checkpoints. We validate both solutions on three benchmarks: Persuasion for Good, tau^2-bench, and CooperBench. Verbalized Sampling improves held-out success by up to 9% over single-simulator RL, and Co-Training pushes gains further to 14%; the human study shows similar gain on real users. Both solutions also preserve the policy diversity that collapses under single-simulator RL. Overall, our findings on simulator collapse point to diverse simulators as a requirement for RL agents that serve real users. We release SCOPE, an open-source framework for Population Co-Training in multi-agent RL.

papers.title_zh: 一个冻结的模拟器并不够：多智能体强化学习中的模拟器坍缩

article.lead: 用大语言模型模拟用户训练智能体，能否让智能体真正适应不同用户？这篇论文指出，依赖单一模拟器可能带来系统性的泛化失败，并探讨如何通过增加模拟行为的多样性缓解这一问题。

sections.title: 单一用户模拟器为何可能误导训练
paragraphs: 在人机交互的多智能体强化学习中，智能体通常与一个模拟用户的大语言模型进行训练。论文指出，这种设置可能出现“模拟器坍塌”：模拟器的输出模式发生坍塌，策略则学会利用这些模式的狭窄行为。
这种策略不一定能适应未见过的模拟器，也可能难以迁移到真实用户。问题因此不只是模拟器能否生成回复，还涉及训练过程中接触到的用户行为是否足够多样。

sections.title: 从回复采样到模拟器共同训练
paragraphs: 论文形式化描述了模拟器坍塌，并提出两种解决方案。**言语化采样**用于推理阶段：先形成以自然语言表述的回复分布，再从中采样每条模拟器回复。
**共同训练**则用于训练阶段，类似自我博弈，让模拟器与策略共同演化，以避免策略利用固定的模式行为。其群体变体从近期检查点池中为每次 rollout 采样模拟器。论文还发布了用于多智能体强化学习中群体共同训练的开源框架 SCOPE。

sections.title: 未见场景的成功率与策略多样性
paragraphs: 作者在 Persuasion for Good、tau^2-bench 和 CooperBench 上验证了两种方案。摘要报告，相比单模拟器强化学习，言语化采样使留出测试成功率最高提升 9%，共同训练将提升进一步推至 14%。
摘要还称，真实用户研究显示了类似幅度的提升；两种方案也保留了在单模拟器强化学习下会坍塌的策略多样性。这些结果支持关注模拟器多样性，但摘要未给出各基准的逐项结果。

sections.title: 摘要尚不能回答哪些验证细节
paragraphs: 摘要没有报告真实用户研究的样本规模与构成，也未说明留出测试的具体划分、各比较方法的完整设置或结果波动。因此，仅凭摘要难以判断不同用户群体、模拟器和任务条件下的效果范围。

sections.title: 阅读启发：检查模拟用户的多样性
paragraphs: 对于使用大语言模型模拟用户的智能体研究，一个值得追问的问题是：策略表现提升是否依赖特定模拟器的行为模式？进一步阅读论文时，可关注留出模拟器与真实用户的比较方式，以及策略多样性的衡量方法。

papers.title: TOUCAN: Synthesizing 1.5M Tool-Agentic Data from Real-World MCP Environments
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are rapidly emerging as powerful systems for automating tasks across domains. Yet progress in the open-source community is constrained by the lack of high quality permissively licensed tool-agentic training data. Existing datasets are limited in diversity, realism, and complexity, particularly regarding multi-tool and multi-turn interactions. To address this gap, we introduce Toucan, which contains 1.5 million trajectories synthesized from nearly 500 real-world Model Context Protocols (MCPs). Unlike prior work, Toucan leverages authentic MCP environments to generate diverse, realistic, and challenging tasks with trajectories involving real tool execution. Our pipeline first produces a broad spectrum of tool-use queries using five distinct models, applies model-based quality filtering, and then generates agentic trajectories with three teacher models using two agentic frameworks. Rigorous rule-based and model-based validation ensures high-quality outputs. We also introduce three extensions to further diversify tasks and simulate multi-turn conversations. Models fine-tuned on Toucan outperform larger closed-source counterparts on the BFCL V3 benchmark and establish a new Pareto optimum on MCP-Universe Bench.

papers.title: Too Many Cooks Spoil The Broth: Auditing Multi-Agent LLM Councils For Medical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Multi-agent debate among large language models (LLMs) is widely assumed to improve reasoning by letting models correct one another. We audit that assumption for English medical question answering (QA). Five open-weight 4 to 8B medical and generalist LLMs answer 8,402 questions across six benchmarks as a council, measured against the same five prompted individually and a single larger Qwen3-VL-32B, text-only. The council beats every member on five of six datasets, but most of that accuracy is in place before debate runs: 67% of verdicts settle at Round 0, and on five of six those are the more accurate questions. Where debate runs, opinion change concentrates on one anchor; on the hardest benchmark 85% of moves toward it happen while it is wrong. There, agreement is worth less than disagreement: questions all five agree on are correct 6.6% of the time against 14.6% otherwise, tracking a shared bias toward the first option. The council also trails the larger model on four of six by up to 16.2 points, at seven times the model calls for 1.6 times the compute. Agreement among models is a measurement that can be biased, not evidence of correctness.
papers.summary: 【摘要】论文审视多智能体辩论是否能改善英语医学问答：五个开放权重模型组成议会，并与各自独立作答及单个更大模型比较。议会在六个数据集中的五个上超过每个成员，但多数裁决在辩论前已确定；最困难基准上，模型意见趋向错误锚点，成员一致也不代表正确。议会在四个数据集上落后于更大模型，同时调用与计算开销更高。摘要未交代完整实验细节，结论的适用范围仍需结合全文核查。[摘要]

papers.title_zh: 厨师过多反而坏事：审视多智能体大语言模型议会的医学推理

article.lead: 多个大模型共同讨论，是否真的能让医学问答更准确？这项研究审视模型间的辩论与共识，提醒读者区分“达成一致”和“答案正确”。

sections.title: 医学问答中的多模型共识可靠吗
paragraphs: 多智能体辩论的常见设想是：让大语言模型相互纠错，从而改善推理。本文针对英语医学问答审视这一假设，关注模型最终答对多少，也关注讨论何时以及如何改变答案。

sections.title: 委员会、独立模型与较大模型的比较
paragraphs: 研究让五个开放权重的医学和通用大语言模型组成委员会，回答六个基准中的 8,402 道问题；这些模型的规模为 4 至 8B。比较对象包括同样五个模型分别接受提示时的表现，以及以纯文本方式使用的单个较大模型 Qwen3-VL-32B。

sections.title: 辩论前已有优势，共识也可能出错
paragraphs: 委员会在六个数据集中的五个上胜过每个成员，但其大部分准确表现并非来自后续辩论：67% 的最终判断在第 0 轮就已确定；在六个数据集中的五个上，这部分问题的准确率更高。
在实际发生辩论的情形中，观点变化集中指向一个锚定对象。在最难的基准上，向该对象靠拢的观点变化有 85% 发生在它给出错误答案时。
同一最难基准中，五个模型全部一致的问题，正确率为 6.6%；未全部一致的问题则为 14.6%。这一现象与模型共同偏向第一个选项有关。模型一致因此可能反映共享偏差，而不能直接充当正确性的证据。
委员会在六个数据集中的四个上落后于较大模型，差距最高达 16.2 个百分点；与此同时，委员会使用了七倍的模型调用和 1.6 倍的计算量。

sections.title: 摘要能支持多大范围的判断
paragraphs: 摘要给出了问题总数、基准数量和模型规模，但未说明各基准的样本构成，也未展开各数据集的完整比较结果。仅凭摘要，无法判断这些发现对其他语言、医学任务或模型组合的适用范围。
摘要也未详述辩论流程、锚定对象的具体定义和验证细节。因此，这里报告的是摘要中的比较与关联，不宜据此推断所有多智能体系统都无效，或将共识偏差归因于某个未说明的机制。

sections.title: 阅读启发：把共识视为待核验的信号
paragraphs: 阅读启发：评估多模型问答时，可以留意最终准确率之外的讨论前后变化，并追问一致意见是否伴随共同偏差。进一步阅读论文时，可重点查看辩论流程、各基准的比较结果以及计算成本的统计方式。

papers.title: TokenCliff: Benchmarking Output-Token Budget Sensitivity in Multi-Turn LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Output-token budgets are a first-order deployment constraint for large language model (LLM) agents, yet existing benchmarks typically evaluate them under a single fixed or generous budget. We introduce TokenCliff, a benchmark for measuring multi-turn agent performance across episode-level output-token budgets. It contains 660 deterministic tasks spanning four capability-oriented domains—file operations, data transformation, tool use, and planning—plus a compositional multi-step split. We propose two budget-sensitivity metrics: Budget Elasticity, which captures robustness across budget levels, and the Cliff Index, which captures the sharpest adjacent-budget performance drop. Evaluating 10 LLMs at five budget levels from 200 to 8,192 tokens yields 33,000 episodes. Results show that (1) accuracy drops by up to 32 percentage points between adjacent budgets; (2) neither peak performance nor larger model size necessarily implies stronger budget elasticity; and (3) budget sensitivity is substantially greater in the evaluated multi-turn setting than in the single-shot diagnostic. Code and data are available in our public repository: https://github.com/BairuiZhang/TokenCliff
papers.summary: 【摘要】论文针对现有智能体基准通常采用单一固定或宽裕预算的问题，提出 TokenCliff，用于衡量多轮智能体在不同单次任务输出词元预算下的表现。基准包含660个确定性任务，并提出预算弹性和悬崖指数两项指标。对10个模型、五档预算的评估显示，相邻预算下准确率最多下降32个百分点；峰值表现或模型规模较大也不必然意味着更强的预算弹性。当前仅能依据摘要判断，无法核查任务细节与实验过程。

article.lead: 大语言模型智能体在多轮任务中能使用多少输出 token，不只是成本设置，也可能影响任务表现。TokenCliff 将输出预算纳入评测，帮助读者关注模型性能随预算变化的稳定性。

sections.title: 智能体评测为何需要关注输出预算
paragraphs: 输出 token 预算是大语言模型智能体部署的重要约束，但摘要指出，现有基准通常只在单一固定预算或较宽裕的预算下评估。这样的评测视角，难以直接呈现性能随预算变化的情况。
TokenCliff 聚焦多轮智能体，以单次任务全过程的输出 token 预算为评测条件，考察不同预算下的任务表现。

sections.title: 从任务集合到预算敏感性指标
paragraphs: 该基准包含 660 个确定性任务，覆盖文件操作、数据转换、工具使用和规划四个能力导向领域，另有一个组合式多步骤划分。
作者提出两个指标：预算弹性（Budget Elasticity）用于刻画跨预算水平的稳健性；悬崖指数（Cliff Index）用于刻画相邻预算之间最剧烈的性能下降。
评测涉及 10 个大语言模型、从 200 到 8,192 tokens 的五个预算水平，共得到 33,000 个评测回合。

sections.title: 相邻预算间也可能出现性能悬崖
paragraphs: 摘要报告，相邻预算水平之间的准确率降幅最高可达 32 个百分点。这提示读者不能仅凭某个预算下的成绩，推断模型在邻近预算下也有相近表现。
研究还发现，峰值表现更好或模型规模更大，并不必然意味着预算弹性更强。在本次评测中，多轮设置的预算敏感性也明显高于单次作答诊断。

sections.title: 摘要尚不能说明的评测边界
paragraphs: 摘要没有列出具体模型、各任务类别的样本构成，也没有说明组合式多步骤划分的具体内容；因此，仅凭摘要无法判断结果对不同任务和模型的适用范围。
摘要没有给出单次作答诊断的具体设置、两项指标的计算细节或其他验证范围。多轮与单次作答的差异应限于所报告的评测条件理解，不能直接推广到所有应用。

sections.title: 阅读启发：把预算曲线纳入模型选择
paragraphs: 对于需要多轮交互的大语言模型应用，阅读启发是：除了比较最高准确率，也可留意不同输出预算下表现是否稳定，以及相邻预算之间是否存在明显落差。
进一步阅读时，可重点查看预算弹性与悬崖指数如何计算、多轮与单次作答如何比较，以及具体任务和模型如何构成；摘要本身尚不足以回答这些问题。

papers.title: T-MAP: Red-Teaming LLM Agents with Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search
papers.abstract: While prior red-teaming efforts have focused on eliciting harmful text outputs from large language models (LLMs), such approaches fail to capture agent-specific vulnerabilities that emerge through multi-step tool execution, particularly in rapidly growing ecosystems such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). To address this gap, we propose a trajectory-aware evolutionary search method, T-MAP, which leverages execution trajectories to guide the discovery of adversarial prompts. Our approach enables the automatic generation of attacks that not only bypass safety guardrails but also reliably realize harmful objectives through actual tool interactions. Empirical evaluations across diverse MCP environments demonstrate that T-MAP substantially outperforms baselines in attack realization rate (ARR) and remains effective against frontier models, including GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, Qwen3.5, and GLM-5, thereby revealing previously underexplored vulnerabilities in autonomous LLM agents. Code is available at https://github.com/pwnhyo/T-MAP.
papers.summary: 论文研究大语言模型智能体在多步工具调用中产生的安全风险，提出轨迹感知进化搜索方法 T-MAP。[P1][P2] 方法结合风险类别与攻击风格档案、跨轨迹诊断和工具调用图，以实际行动完成程度评价攻击。[P3][P4] 作者报告其在五种 MCP 环境中的平均攻击实现率为57.8%，并通过消融、多模型及人工评价补充证据。[P5][P7][P8] 结果受沙箱环境和攻击者模型等条件限制，不能直接等同于真实部署风险。[P9]
papers.method: 基于原文摘要的规则摘要
papers.recommendation: 建议从事工具调用智能体安全评估的读者重点阅读：论文不仅提供可复核的搜索框架和轨迹级指标，还报告消融、重复实验与人工评价；但迁移到实际业务前应关注沙箱和裁判可靠性限制。[P4][P7][P9][P13]

deep_read.problem: 论文关注传统红队测试难以覆盖的智能体风险：有害后果可能由规划、连续工具调用和环境反馈共同产生，而非单轮文本直接显现。[P1] 作者因此把评估重点转向工具执行是否完成预期有害行动，并区分拒绝、执行错误、部分完成和完全实现。[P5]
deep_read.method: T-MAP 按风险类别与攻击风格维护二维精英档案，保存候选提示及其轨迹。[P3] 每轮从父轨迹提取成功因素、从目标轨迹诊断失败原因，结合记录工具转换结果的有向图生成候选；执行后由裁判评估并更新档案与图。[P4][P21]
deep_read.innovation: 相对仅依据文本反馈或单个单元经验进行提示改写，作者将跨单元成功与失败诊断和工具调用图结合，分别提供提示层面及行动层面的搜索信号。[P4] 解读：其方法特点在于复用跨轨迹经验，同时显式维护工具转换结果，而非仅追求单个成功提示。
deep_read.findings: 主实验中，T-MAP 在五种 MCP 环境均取得最高攻击实现率，平均为57.8%。[P5] 消融实验中，移除工具调用图使 L3 从58.40%降至45.71%；移除交叉诊断使拒绝率从11.93%升至15.63%。[P8] 三种随机种子实验也支持其相对优势，但不同表格的结果应分别引用。[P13]
deep_read.limitations: 作者指出实验仅覆盖五类 MCP 服务器，且在沙箱中进行，现实权限检查等保护可能限制结果外推；攻击者模型的安全对齐也会影响效果。[P9] 人工标为 L3 的评价中有29.8%被模型判为 L2。[P12] 核对记录未报告原文件缺项；所列编码提取错误已纠正，不构成公式缺失。
deep_read.connection: 解读：对采用工具调用智能体的智能运维，本文的轨迹分级和转换图可启发审查权限变更、文件操作及跨工具链的风险，而不只检查回复文本。[P4][P24] 但资料未验证其在工业运维中的效果，也未提供结构设计或工程可靠性领域的直接实验。
deep_read.next_steps: 建议在授权沙箱内构建贴近实际运维流程的测试集，区分工具调用成功、关键步骤完成与真实业务后果，并比较权限确认等防护措施的影响。[P9][P20] 建议增加人工复核与多攻击者模型重复实验，报告裁判分歧和结果波动，而非仅依赖单一平均指标。[P12][P13]
